correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the Zak diagonalization of the integer-modulation Gabor operator for g=(1−|x|)_+, translations k/q, q>=2, modulation m. The scalar multiplier is Φ=q−2c_q(t)+2c_q(t)cos(2πω) with c_q piecewise quadratic and q strict nondegenerate maxima. Its reciprocal has Fourier coefficients (−r_q(t))^|n|/Δ_q(t), where Δ=√[q(q−4c)] and r=(q−Δ)/(q+Δ). Multiplying by Zg(t,ω)=(1−t)+te^{2πiω} yields γ_q(t+n)=(−r)^n[1−t(1+r)]/Δ. Laplace expansion at the q maxima yields I_n∼E_q R_q^(2n)/√n with positive E_q; reflection symmetry and a geometrically weighted tail yield 2E_q/(1−R_q²). Domain fixed q>=2, n→∞; no uniform-q bound. I independently numerically integrated cells at n=25,80,250 for q=2,3,4,7. Ratios to asymptotic tend to unity, e.g q2: 0.9967864,0.9990145,0.9996866; q3: 0.9961467,0.9988089,0.9996202. Finite quadrature is not proof of the asymptotic.
